newsitem.title: FRANCE: French truckers sign partial deal with bosses.
newsitem.headline: French truckers sign partial deal with bosses.

text.p: French truck drivers' unions signed a partial agreement with employers on Friday, a government mediator said, but talks were continuing on the unresolved issues of pay and working hours and 225 roadblocks stayed in place across France.

Mediator Robert Cros told reporters the negotiators had signed five agreements covering retirement at 55 instead of 60, sick pay, travel expenses, union rights and a ban on Sunday driving. But the unions did not sign a draft agreement on work time and negotiations were continuing, he said.
Cros said Transport Minister Bernard Pons had instructed him to chair a supervisory committee "to ensure what is signed is actually implemented".

He said the government would put to the parties "in the coming hours for very rapid signature" a draft decree abolishing longstanding practices whereby truckers are paid for fewer hours than they actually work or are on standby.
"As for the definition of working time, the government has appointed me to to work out a solution by December 15 with the parties," Cros said. "This subject will also be the object of a decree."

The unions have maintained their stranglehold on French roads and fuel supplies to win higher pay and shorter working hours. They did not call for a return to work after signing the partial agreement.
